subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static vehicle model as a single TypeScript module, deciding to skip joints since it's static and simple plain objects with positioned parts will work fine, laying out the design along the Z-axis.

I'm sketching the proportions: a ten-meter hull with six wheels across three axles, a twin-rail railgun turret with a long barrel on top, and four deployable outrigger stabilizer legs touching the ground. I'm figuring out helper functions for boxes, using mottled paint patterns for the hull from the clockwork kit, a glow kit for the rail coils and lights, and SVG textures for emblems, warning chevrons, and stencils, while working out how to orient the cylindrical wheels correctly.

Still designing wheel details...

Now I'm working out the hull geometry using an extruded side profile: plotting a polygon in the z-y plane for the body outline (rear, cab, hood) and extruding it along x with centered thickness to form the main chassis shape.

Wheels sit outside the hull at that offset so they clear the body, with fenders arching over them. I'm positioning a windscreen plane angled along the cab's slope, tilting its normal to face up and forward to match the roofline.

Now I'm laying out the front end details—headlight housings, bumper, tow hooks, plate—then moving to the railgun mount: a turret ring on the rear deck, a lathe-based cradle base, a turret body box, and twin rail barrels extending forward from the mount.

I'm sizing the barrel rails and adding glow strips along their inner faces, then working out how to represent the coil rings around the barrel using small boxes instead of a full lathe shape to avoid blocking the gap between rails.

For detailing I'm planning a muzzle brake with slots, a breech block box at the rear, and cylindrical capacitor banks on the turret sides with banded textures and glowing end caps, connected to the breech via swept cable curves using catmull points. I'm also deciding to keep the barrel mostly horizontal rather than adding elevation tilt.

Now I'm figuring out the stabilizer legs and wheel placements, checking axle positions and radii to find clear gaps on the hull where the outrigger arms can extend without colliding with the wheels.

Still writing strut geometry...

Now I'm planning surface details: roof hatches, antenna, sensor mast, searchlight, emblem decals and stencil numbers placed on offset side planes, plus a handful of textures for hazard stripes, screens, glass, and vents. I'm also sketching in tool boxes, fuel cans, an exhaust stack, rear vents, a rear ladder, and armor plating for added realism.

For the panel bolts, I'm deciding against using bone-based path placement since there's no bone structure here, and opting instead for simple loops to compute bolt positions directly before merging all the geometries together.

Part counts should stay manageable without merging—wheels contribute roughly 150 parts and the total model around 450, so I'll keep segment counts low to control triangle counts. For colors, I'm settling on a flat palette under 64 entries: olive, dark, steel, chrome, and yellow tones.

Writing helper functions...

With a large hull area, texel density gets coarse enough that fine rivets and seams may vanish, so bumping paint resolution only partially helps — I'll lean on simpler mottle-and-countershade paint rather than fine panel detail to keep things readable at that scale.

Importing the steel and iron metal presets from the clockwork kit for rails and chrome, then working out armour panel placement along the hull sides, positioning raised boxes around the wheel zone and cab area without clashing with the fenders.

Now I'm adding wheel fenders with mudguard flaps, a chevron texture on the leg arms, and front details — glowing headlight boxes flanking a front bumper with chevron striping.

For the rear I'm planning a bumper, red tail light glows, a ladder, vertical exhaust stacks, a cargo box, and vented deck panels with upward-facing texture planes. I'm also working out the railgun turret placement, centering it on the deck and lathing a ring base for the mount.

I'm figuring out the turret body as an extruded iron-colored profile with chamfered edges spanning the vertical range, then deciding the rail positions need to clear the turret top so they don't end up buried inside the geometry.

Still positioning cradle trunnions and rail clamps...

Positioning glow strips between the rails leaving a small gap, and checking the rail extents against the breech and turret placement to make sure everything lines up without overlap.

Now I'm placing the coil segments along the barrel, each with top and bottom bars plus glow nodes, and figuring out cable sweeps from capacitors down to the breech. I'm also sizing the capacitor cylinders and checking their position fits within the hull and turret ring without clipping, then adding thicker band rings around them.

Next I'm routing the cables with smooth curves from the capacitor tips to the breech using thin dark sweeps, then moving on to the sensor mast setup on the cab roof—mounting a radome sphere, antenna rods, a searchlight, and a glowing light bar, plus planning the side window placement on the cab.

I'm positioning the side window glass panels on the hull, checking they fit within the sloped cab profile without clipping, then working out placement for the "RG-6 HELIOS" emblem decal while avoiding overlap with the armor panel geometry on the sides.

I'm positioning the turret ring, rear deck vents, cargo hatch, and exhaust stacks at the hull's rear corners, then planning tail details like the bumper, lights, hitch, and ladder rods. Now I'm working out the outrigger leg placement on each side at the front and rear z-positions.

Still writing outrigger geometry...

Adding hazard chevron plane to the arm front face and sketching the wheel builder function — tyre cylinder, tread blocks arranged radially, rim and hub pieces.

I'm now planning the outer wheel face as a textured circle with rim dish, spokes, and bolt pattern, with lug nuts added as separate 3D elements on top for depth, positioned along the x-axis offset from the hub.

For the tread blocks, I'm working out rotation math so each box aligns radially around the tire circumference — rotating about the x-axis by the block's angular position so it faces outward correctly in world space.

Now I'm adding mud texturing to the tires, blending a dark rubber color with a muddy tone near the bottom using noise and smoothstep for a weathered look. I'm also sketching out the hull's underbody and skirt — a dark box beneath the main hull for the belly, and cylindrical axle boxes spanning the vehicle's width to connect the wheels.

I'm planning the front details: a grille plane positioned on the face above the bumper, headlights placed symmetrically, and the sloped hood with vent boxes. I'm listing out the textures I'll need — glass, grille, chevron markings, emblem, stenciled text, wheel treads, and vents — then starting to write the SVG for the glass texture with a gradient fill.

Writing more texture SVGs...

Writing hull and turret extrusion code...

I should also add mudflaps, tow shackles, and jerrycans on the rear deck, plus hood vents and bolt rows, aiming for roughly 400 lines total. I'll add a bolt helper for panel corners and an orange glow warning light on the cab roof, making sure imports stay clean and unused ones are removed.
